title: Would a Large Language Model Pay Extra for a View? Inferring Willingness to Pay from Subjective Choices

bias_targets.methodology: Swapping the presentation order of the hotel room alternatives (A and B) in the choice dilemmas and using alternative-specific constants in multinomial logit models to detect if the LLM systematically favors the first presented option.

Evaluating willingness-to-pay (WTP) estimates for attributes with varying description lengths and re-testing with truncated descriptive text to demonstrate how detailed phrasing disproportionately inflates the model's valuations.

Injecting different user background profiles (e.g., a budget-conscious student versus a comfort-seeking business traveler) into the prompts to measure shifts in willingness-to-pay and to detect extreme, one-dimensional stereotypical decision-making behavior.
